info.title: countdown store contract
info.description: What the broker (the config site) and the renderers (the providers and the render pool) keep in the Redis they share, which is all they say to each other: the keys and channels, what each holds, its TTL, who writes it and who reads it, the scripts both sides run, and canonical examples (countdown_api/fixtures) that both sides' tests and this repository's check against.

sources.weather: Weather keys (WeatherKey): the place picked on the settings page by name, country and Open-Meteo id (london-gb-2643743), or the slug of a typed location (london). The members are the <key> of v1:weather:<key>, and a screen's config carries its own as weather.key.
sources.glow: Device ids with a Glowmarkt account the broker's glow provider signs in with.
sources.spotify: Device ids with Spotify (or Apple Music) switched on.
sources.developer: Device ids with the developer panel switched on.
sources.parcel: Device ids with parcels switched on (an e-paper screen's or a touchscreen's), so a Parcel API key saved.
sources.postcode: The notice board's place: every screen's postcode in the broker's canonical form ("SW1A 1AA", or "0150" for a Norwegian one, which is four digits), for the providers of notices about a place (floods, weather warnings, roads). Never logged.
sources.background: Weather keys (WeatherKey) of the places the paired touchscreens show, a subset of `weather`'s: the places the background provider makes pictures for. An e-paper screen draws no background, so its place isn't here. Each member has a v1:background-place:<key> beside it, written in the same transaction.

subscription.written_by: the broker, on every config save, rebuilt whole from its database in one transaction
subscription.read_by: the providers, each its own source's
subscription.description: The ids some screen wants from `source`, replaced atomically (DEL then SADD in one transaction) whenever a config is saved, then a nudge on sub_changed. A missing key is an empty set.

sub_changed.written_by: the broker, after replacing the subscriptions
sub_changed.read_by: every provider, so it needn't wait for its next tick
sub_changed.description: A pub/sub channel, not a key; the message is empty.

config.written_by: the broker, from its database on every config save, as it starts and every minute
config.description: A paired screen's config, with no pairing code (null) and no secret of any kind. A missing key means there's nothing to render: a device not paired, or with a pairing code to show (pairing).

pairing.ttl: the code's own expiry, ten minutes from when it was issued (set with PXAT to the millisecond). The broker deletes it sooner when the code is used, or the device paired, unpaired or forgotten.
pairing.written_by: the broker, whenever it issues a pairing code
pairing.read_by: the render pool, for the pairing screen
pairing.description: While a device has a pairing code to show: its config with `pairing_code` set (there's no config key then). Plaintext by decision: any Redis reader on the host can see a live code. Never logged.

render_screens.written_by: the broker, whole, wherever it differs, whenever it writes the configs
render_screens.read_by: the render pool (the ticker, and the claim script's HGET, which drops a job for any other)
render_screens.description: The screens the render pool draws: device id to slug, the slug naming the screen in the pool's metrics (their `device` label).

render_jobs.written_by: the enqueue script, run by the broker and the render pool alike
render_jobs.description: The render pool's job queue, of device ids; a screen is in it at most once (render_queued).

render_queued.ttl: the ticker's minute, so a worker that dies between the pop and the claim keeps the screen out of the queue for no longer than that.
render_queued.read_by: the claim script, which deletes it
render_queued.description: That a job for the screen is in the queue, holding when it was queued (Redis's clock).

frame.ttl: a day from the last change: a render whose frame is the record's (its etag) writes nothing and doesn't renew it.
frame.written_by: the render pool, whole in one transaction, when the picture changes
frame.read_by: the broker, which serves it to the screen
frame.description: A screen's latest frame, its ETag and when it was first drawn.

energy.description: A Glow device's electricity use, as Glowmarkt gave it.

spotify.description: What a device's Spotify and Apple Music are playing, and what's up next. While Spotify plays, the music provider rewrites it every few seconds (with `spotify_playback` fresh, and the queue only when it is due or the track changed), asks for a faster refresh with `v1:pace:spotify:<device id>` and queues a render of the screen.

spotify_top.description: A device's Spotify and Apple Music top tracks and artists. Apart from the player's key because it's fetched far less often (every half hour) and kept far longer.

params.url: the image's URL as the music service gave it; the key holds its SHA1 in hex.

album_art.ttl: renewed every minute a spotify key still shows it.
album_art.description: An album's cover, by its URL, so every screen showing the same album reads one copy: the image file's own bytes, as the service serves it (the smallest of its sizes at least 120 px tall, else the tallest).

developer.description: A device's developer panel data (GitHub summary and AI plans).

parcels.ttl: twelve hours, so the last answer outlasts the night, when the provider doesn't poll; a screen then shows a parcel's last known state rather than nothing, and `fetched_at` says how old it is. Rewritten (and so renewed) on every poll that gets an answer.
parcels.read_by: the parcels panel and its parcel notices, the broker's `getNotices`
parcels.description: A device's active deliveries from the Parcel app, in the owner's own Parcel account, normalised to ParcelList. Parcels the provider has seen delivered stay in it for a few hours (it drops them after that), so the screen can show that they arrived. A missing key means no answer yet, or the key lapsed: the panel shows its standard data-not-available state.

parcels_status.ttl: a day, renewed on every poll that reaches Parcel. `invalid_key` isn't renewed, as the provider stops polling the key until its config is saved again, so it lapses to a missing key a day later.
parcels_status.read_by: the broker, for the link status on the config page
parcels_status.description: Whether the device's Parcel API key works: `ok`, `invalid_key` (Parcel answered 401) or `rate_limited`. A missing key means the provider hasn't tried it yet.

params.item_id: what it fetched, e.g. a device id.

pace.ttl: renewed each cycle the provider still wants it; so it lapses by itself when the provider stops, or dies.
pace.written_by: any provider whose data is bursty (the provider runner, the broker's developer and music providers)
pace.read_by: the broker, which paces the screen's polls
pace.description: The seconds a provider wants the screen to poll at while what it fetched for `item_id` is bursty.

params.stop_id: the stop's id at its source (DepartureStop's id), TfL's and Entur's sharing the namespace.

departures.written_by: countdown's TfL and Entur providers, for every stop in v1:sub:tfl and v1:sub:entur
departures.read_by: the arrivals panels, and the broker's getArrivals
departures.description: A stop's next departures, soonest first, whichever country and mode. A stop with nothing due is still written, with no departures, so "nothing due" isn't taken for "no data".

params.weather_key: the place's weather key (WeatherKey), as the config has it in weather.key.

weather.written_by: countdown's weather provider, for every key in v1:sub:weather
weather.read_by: the weather panel, and the broker's getWeather
weather.description: A place's Open-Meteo forecast, as fetched: not the panel's pages, which the renderer works out from it when it draws, so "now" and "tonight" are as of drawing.

params.weather_key: the place's weather key (WeatherKey), as the config has it in weather.key.

background.ttl: renewed with each image written to it.
background.written_by: countdown's background provider, for every key in v1:sub:background
background.description: A place's backgrounds for the weather panel: one AI-made photo per part of the day (dawn, day, dusk, night), each made shortly before its part starts from the forecast for that hour, so the list fills in through the day. Every screen on the same weather key shows the same pictures.

params.digest: the image's SHA-256 (BackgroundDigest), in lower-case hex.

background_image.written_by: countdown's background provider, beside v1:background:<weather key>
background_image.description: A background's own bytes (a JPEG), by its SHA-256, so its address names the picture and not the place, and never changes for the same bytes.

params.weather_key: the place's weather key (WeatherKey), a member of v1:sub:background.

background_place.written_by: the broker, with the subscriptions and in their transaction, for every member of v1:sub:background; it deletes those of the members that left
background_place.description: What the background provider needs to know of a place that its weather key doesn't say: what to call it in a picture's prompt, its country, and the postcodes of the notice boards of the touchscreens showing it, whose weather warnings the picture may show. A member of v1:sub:background with none is left out until it has one.

params.stop_id: a TfL stop's NaPTAN id from v1:sub:tfl.

tfl_line_status.read_by: the notice board, and the broker's getNotices
tfl_line_status.description: The status of every line serving a TfL stop, Good Service too, as TfL's /Line/{ids}/Status answers it. A stop that isn't a bus stop or Tube station is written with no lines.

params.stop_id: a TfL stop's NaPTAN id from v1:sub:tfl.

tfl_stations.read_by: the notice board, and the broker's getNotices
tfl_stations.description: What's wrong at a TfL stop (lifts out of order, closed entrances...), as TfL's /StopPoint/{id}/Disruption answers it, expired entries and all.

params.postcode: a postcode from v1:sub:postcode, as the broker writes it ("SE17 3LL").

tfl_roads.written_by: countdown's TfL notices provider, for every UK postcode in v1:sub:postcode
tfl_roads.read_by: the notice board, and the broker's getNotices
tfl_roads.description: The road disruptions TfL reports near the postcode's place. TfL only knows London's roads, so elsewhere it's always empty.

tfl_network.written_by: countdown's TfL notices provider, with no subscription, as every London device reads it
tfl_network.description: The status of every Tube line and the Elizabeth line, Good Service too, as TfL's /Line/Mode/tube,elizabeth-line/Status answers it: the network at a glance, for a touchscreen with nothing on its notice board.

params.postcode: a UK postcode from v1:sub:postcode, as the broker writes it ("SE17 3LL").

met_office.written_by: countdown's Met Office provider, for every UK postcode in v1:sub:postcode
met_office.read_by: the notice board, and the broker's getNotices
met_office.description: The Met Office's weather warnings for the postcode's place: its warning region's RSS feed, its items as the feed has them. Their severity, area and times are in the items' text; the notice board works them out when it draws.

bank_holidays.written_by: countdown's bank holidays provider, with no subscription, as every UK device reads it
bank_holidays.read_by: the notice board, and the broker's getNotices
bank_holidays.description: gov.uk's bank holidays for every part of the UK (https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json), by its divisions.

args: the queued flag's TTL in ms (RENDER_QUEUED_TTL_MS)
enqueue.returns: 1 if it queued the screen, 0 if it was queued already.
enqueue.description: Queue a render of a screen unless one is queued already: SET the queued flag NX with its TTL (to Redis's clock, in Unix ms), and only if that set it, LPUSH the device id onto the jobs. So a screen is in the queue at most once however many ask.

post.description: The secret the device generated and keeps becomes a device of its type at once (201); only its hash is stored, and identifies the device. A repeat, e.g. on every boot, is a 200 and changes nothing. Throttled per IP, as anyone can call it (429 with Retry-After), and refused (503 with Retry-After) while too many devices wait to be paired.

200.description: A device already registered with that secret.

400.description: A registration the schema doesn't allow.

429.description: Too many registrations from this IP; try again after Retry-After.

503.description: Too many devices waiting to be paired; try again after Retry-After.

get.description: The device's config, as v1:config:<device id> holds it (ConfigResponse); for an e-paper screen no one has paired, the pairing value instead (v1:pairing:<device id>: the config with the code to show, which the server issues afresh as each expires), as the render pool gets for its pairing screen. A touchscreen is paired by token and never has a code. The server is the one source of truth for it; the device keeps a copy of the last one it got for when the server can't be reached. Its version comes as the ETag, which a save sends back as If-Match; with If-None-Match of the version the caller has, it's a 304 while that is still the config. The settings site (APP_HOST) reads it too, with the person's login instead of a secret, for the device its `device_id` names.

parameters.name: device_id
parameters.description: On the settings site only, with the person's login instead of the secret: which of their devices. A device sends no `device_id`: its secret says which it is.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: The ETag of the copy the caller has.

200.description: The config, with an e-paper screen's `pairing_code` set while it is to show one.

ETag.description: The config's version, quoted (ConfigVersion), to send back as If-Match.

304.description: The config is still the version If-None-Match names.

ETag.description: The config's version, quoted (ConfigVersion), to send back as If-Match.

401.description: A missing or unknown secret, or, on the settings site, no login.

404.description: On the settings site, not one of the signed-in person's devices.

put.description: What a device with a settings panel of its own (a touchscreen) saves when its owner changes something there: the whole config, as it got it with the change made. The read-only fields (readOnly) are the server's or the device's registration's and can't be changed here: they're sent as they came, and anything else is a 400. Answers the config as saved, as GET does. With If-Match, saved only while the config is still that version. A section at a time is putConfigSection, which the settings site uses too.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag of the config the change was made to; a stale one is a 409, and nothing is saved.

ETag.description: The config's version, quoted (ConfigVersion), to send back as If-Match.

400.description: A config the schema doesn't allow, or one that changes a read-only field.

409.description: The device isn't paired yet, so there's no owner's config to save; or If-Match is stale: someone saved in between, so read the config again.

put.summary: Save one section of the device's config, whole.
put.description: Replaces one section of the config (ConfigSection) with the one sent, whole: there's no saving a field on its own. The server puts it into the config as it stands, checks the result against the device type's schema (EpaperConfig or TouchscreenConfig), saves it, and answers the whole config as saved, with its new version. If-Match is required, the ETag of the config the change was made to: when someone has saved since, it's a 409 and nothing is saved, so read the config again (getConfig) rather than overwrite theirs. What the server works out itself is answered as it works it out, whatever was sent: the notice board's `country` (from the postcode, which it writes in its usual form) and the weather's `location` (the name of the place whose key is sent). A weather `key` is one a place search answered (searchPlaces' `value`), or the one saved; null, with an empty `location`, clears the place. A service's `enabled` is saved as sent, but answered as on only while the owner's account has the login or key it needs. A device saves its own config only if it's a paired touchscreen; on the settings site, with the person's login instead of the secret, any device of theirs, named by `device_id`.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: The section to replace; one the device's type doesn't have is a 404.

parameters.name: device_id
parameters.description: On the settings site only, with the person's login instead of the secret: which of their devices. A device sends no `device_id`: its secret says which it is.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag of the config the change was made to (getConfig's, or the last save's).

requestBody.description: The section's new value, in its own schema: the field's in ConfigBase, or for `style`, `display` and `lyrics`, the device type's own (EpaperStyle or TouchscreenStyle, TouchscreenDisplay, TouchscreenLyrics).

ETag.description: The config's version, quoted (ConfigVersion), to send back as If-Match.

400.description: A value the section's schema doesn't allow, or that makes a config the device type's schema doesn't: an unknown weather key, a postcode that isn't a UK or Norwegian one, a stop whose source isn't its id's; or, on the settings site, no `device_id`.

401.description: A missing or unknown secret, or, on the settings site, no login.

403.description: The device saving its own config isn't a paired touchscreen, or its owner doesn't approve the save.

404.description: A section the device's type doesn't have; or, on the settings site, not one of the signed-in person's devices.

409.description: If-Match is stale (someone saved in between), so read the config again; nothing was saved.

503.description: The weather place couldn't be checked with Open-Meteo just now; try again shortly.

get.summary: Search for stations and stops to show departures from.
get.description: London's (TfL) and Norway's (Entur) stops matching the text, asked at once: Norway's first when the text has æ, ø or å, London's first otherwise. A Norwegian station is followed by its platforms (or stop poles), indented under it. Each result's `value` is the stop as the config's arrivals has it, to add to `arrivals.stops`. On the settings site (APP_HOST) it takes the person's login instead of a secret.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The text to search for; under 2 characters (after trimming) answers no results.

200.description: The results, best first, possibly none.

401.description: A missing or unknown secret, or, on the settings site, no login.

502.description: Neither TfL nor Entur could be asked; the body is no results.

get.summary: Search for a town or city for the weather.
get.description: The places Open-Meteo's geocoding finds for the name, best first (the first is the one the weather would find for that name too). Each result's `value` is the config's weather section for that place, to save whole as `weather`. On the settings site (APP_HOST) it takes the person's login instead of a secret.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The name to search for; under 2 characters (after trimming) answers no results.

200.description: The results, best first, possibly none.

401.description: A missing or unknown secret, or, on the settings site, no login.

502.description: Open-Meteo couldn't be asked; the body is no results.

get.summary: An access token for the owner's Spotify, for a touchscreen.
get.description: A short-lived Spotify access token for the account that owns the touchscreen, in Spotify's own token shape, for its Web Playback SDK and Web API calls. The Spotify link is the account's (its Account page); the server keeps the refresh token and the app's secret, and renews the access token itself, so neither ever reaches a device. Ask again before expires_in runs out. Only a paired touchscreen gets one.

403.description: The account linked Spotify before touchscreens could use it, so its link lacks the scopes they need (SpotifyAccessToken's scope); linking it again on the Account page grants them.

404.description: The owner's account hasn't linked Spotify.

409.description: The device isn't paired yet, or isn't a touchscreen.

502.description: Spotify couldn't be reached, or refused to renew the token.

get.description: The forecast for the device's weather place (its config's weather.key), as the store has it: current conditions (is_day among them), the hourly forecast and each day's sunrise and sunset, in the place's local time. Read from the store alone, so it's as fresh as the weather provider's last fetch (fetched_at); forecast is null while there's none.

409.description: The device isn't paired yet, so it has no config to read.

503.description: The store couldn't be reached; try again shortly.

get.description: The next departures from each of the device's stops (its config's arrivals.stops), in the owner's order, as the store has them: each stop's soonest first, with its expected time rather than seconds to go. A stop with nothing stored is listed with null departures.

409.description: The device isn't paired yet, so it has no config to read.

503.description: The store couldn't be reached; try again shortly.

get.description: What the store has for the device's notice board: the status of the lines at its TfL stops and the disruptions there, TfL's road disruptions, the Met Office's warnings near its postcode, the UK's bank holidays and, with parcels switched on, its owner's parcels. Each as its provider stored it (DeviceNotices), not worded or judged as notices.

409.description: The device isn't paired yet, so it has no config to read.

503.description: The store couldn't be reached; try again shortly.

get.summary: The device's weather, arrivals and notices, live.
get.description: A server-sent event stream (text/event-stream) of what getWeather, getArrivals and getNotices answer, so a touchscreen's panels update without polling: each as an event named for it (`weather`, `arrivals`, `notices`) whose data is that route's answer as JSON (DeviceFeedEvent), all three as the stream opens and then each again whenever it changes. A comment line (`: ping`) every 15 s keeps it open through proxies; one that goes quiet for longer has dropped. The server ends the stream after about ten minutes, and when the store goes down, and the device opens it again (its `retry` field says after how long). It takes the device's secret in the Authorization header like every route, so a device reads it with fetch rather than EventSource, which can't send one.

409.description: The device isn't paired yet, so it has no config to read.

503.description: The store couldn't be reached; try again shortly.

get.description: A background's JPEG (v1:background-image:<digest>), by the SHA-256 that getWeather's background names it by. The same digest is always the same bytes, so it's answered with Cache-Control immutable and a year's max-age.

404.description: No such image, or it has expired.

get.summary: Register a touchscreen and make the person signed in on it its owner.
get.description: The page a touchscreen opens to register through the login, in place of a pairing code: by the time the request arrives the person has signed in (or signed up), and the one visit registers the touchscreen and claims it for them. The tablet sends only its secret's hash (SecretHash), so the secret is never in a URL; it then calls the devices' API with the secret itself, paired from its first call. With `return_to`, the page redirects there once it's done (303), adding `device_id`, or `error=taken` when someone else owns the touchscreen. A visit the browser says came from another site (Sec-Fetch-Site), or that doesn't say, changes nothing and answers a page that asks to confirm, which posts the same fields from this site. Throttled per IP.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: A URL of the tablet's own app to come back to once registered, on one of the origins the server allows (its setting TOUCHSCREEN_RETURN_ORIGINS); any other is a 400, before anything is registered.

200.description: A page saying the touchscreen is theirs (also for a repeat), or, for a visit from another site, the page that asks to confirm.

303.description: Back to `return_to`, with `device_id` (registered, or theirs already) or `error=taken`.

400.description: A hash, size or return URL that isn't one (a return URL must be on an origin the server allows).

409.description: Someone else owns the touchscreen (with no `return_to`; with one, a 303 with `error=taken`).

429.description: Too many registrations from this IP; try again after Retry-After.

post.summary: Confirm a touchscreen's registration from the page that asks to.
post.description: What the confirming page posts, from this site only: the same fields as the GET's query, and the same answers.

200.description: A page saying the touchscreen is theirs.

400.description: A hash, size or return URL that isn't one.

409.description: Someone else owns the touchscreen (with no `return_to`).

429.description: Too many registrations from this IP; try again after Retry-After.

get.summary: The settings page of one of the signed-in person's devices.
get.description: The device's settings, as its owner sees them on the settings site; a device that isn't theirs is a 404. With `embed=1` the page has no site navigation and no list of their screens, only the page itself, for a frame in the device's own settings, and its forms and redirects keep `embed=1`. A frame only has the person's login when the page around it is on the same site as the settings site (the login's cookies are SameSite=Lax); without it the frame gets the login's redirect, which the login provider refuses to show in a frame.

parameters.name: embed
parameters.description: 1 for the page without the site around it, to show in a frame.

404.description: No such device, or not one of the signed-in person's.

deviceSecret.description: The secret the device registered with (DeviceRegistration), as Authorization: Bearer <secret>.

DeviceId.description: A device's id, 12 hex digits (six random bytes), as the broker registered it.

Subscription.description: A subscription set's members, in no order. See `sources` for each source's.

SubChanged.description: The nudge on v1:sub:changed carries nothing.

RenderScreens.description: v1:render:screens, device id to the screen's slug.

RenderJobs.description: v1:render:jobs, device ids, newest first (LPUSH; the workers BRPOP the oldest).

RenderQueuedFlag.description: When the job was queued, in Unix milliseconds by Redis's clock (TIME), as decimal text.

FrameRecord.description: The fields of the v1:frame:<device id> hash, all of them always there.

frame.description: The panel's 48,000 bytes (800x480 at one bit a pixel), as the screen takes them. Raw, not base64.

etag.description: The frame's 8-byte BLAKE2b in hex, the ETag the broker serves it with (in quotes), whichever copy it serves.

rendered_at.description: When this picture was first written, ISO 8601 in UTC to the millisecond, e.g. 2026-10-18T12:00:00.000+00:00. It doesn't move while the picture stays the same.

StoredEnergy.description: The value of v1:energy:<device id>: Glowmarkt's own readings answers, as the broker got them, in a thin wrapper. Each page's readings run from the start of its window's first bucket as of fetched_at (the hour 24 hours before, midnight 31 days before, 1st January) to fetched_at; the renderer cuts each to its window when it draws.

offset.description: Glowmarkt's `offset` parameter the readings were asked for with: minutes to add to local time to get UTC, so BST is "-60".

resource_id.description: The meter's "electricity consumption" resource the readings are of.

GlowmarktReadings.description: Glowmarkt's answer to GET /resource/<id>/readings, as it gave it: its `data` is [Unix seconds, kWh] pairs. The renderer reads it with its own model of Glowmarkt's answer.

StoredPlayer.description: The value of v1:spotify:<device id>. Each service's part is in Spotify's own shape (/me/player/queue: its currently_playing, null when nothing plays, and its queue; Apple Music's made to look like it, from the last played track and the ones before it), null when the service is off for the device or couldn't be fetched. `spotify_playback` is how far into the track Spotify was, which is fetched far more often than the queue while something plays (see the `pace` key), so it has a time of its own.

SpotifyPlayback.description: Where Spotify's player was, from /me/player/currently-playing, as of `fetched_at`. While `is_playing`, the position at a later time is `progress_ms` plus the time since `fetched_at`. `track_id` is the id of the track it was in (null for one without an id, a local file), so a reader can tell whether `spotify.currently_playing` is that track or an older one. Null or missing when nothing plays or Spotify is off.

MusicQueue.description: Spotify's /me/player/queue answer (or Apple Music's, made to look like it), as the provider got it.

StoredTop.description: The value of v1:spotify-top:<device id>: each service's top lists by Spotify's time range ("long_term", "short_term"), each its /me/top/tracks and /me/top/artists answers, null when the service is off for the device or couldn't be fetched.

MusicTopLists.description: A service's top lists by Spotify's time range ("long_term", "short_term").

MusicTopRange.description: A service's top tracks and artists over one time range, as its /top/tracks and /top/artists answer.

StoredDeveloper.description: The value of v1:developer:<device id>: the GitHub summary (null until the owner adds a GitHub token) and the AI plans, as the broker's services/developer.py builds them.

ParcelStatus.description: Where a delivery is, normalised from Parcel's status codes by the provider; nothing downstream sees those codes. `ordered` is a delivery the carrier hasn't collected, `exception` one that needs the owner's attention (failed attempt, held, returned) and `unknown` a code the provider has no mapping for.

Parcel.description: One active delivery in the owner's Parcel account.

description.description: What the owner called the delivery in Parcel (or what Parcel made of it).

carrier.description: The carrier's name, as Parcel gives it (Royal Mail, DHL, Amazon).

expected_date.description: The day the carrier expects to deliver, in the owner's time zone, null when it hasn't said. Optional, so a provider that doesn't know it can leave it out.

updated_at.description: When Parcel last saw the delivery change.

ParcelList.description: The value of v1:parcels:<device id>: the owner's active deliveries and when they were fetched. Ordered by expected date, soonest first, those with none last; the panel does not have to sort them.

ParcelsLinkStatus.description: Whether Parcel took the device's API key at the last poll; the value of v1:parcels-status:<device id>.

AlbumArt.description: An image file's own bytes (a JPEG, as the music service serves it).

Pace.description: Seconds, as decimal text (what SET of an integer stores).

WeatherKey.description: A weather key. For a place picked on the settings page it is the slug of its name, its country (xx for none) and its Open-Meteo id, or just the country and id for a name with no Latin letters; for a typed location, that text's slug. weather_keys.json has examples.

ConfigVersion.description: A config's version, as an HTTP ETag (quoted): it changes whenever anything in the config does, and only then. getConfig answers it, and a save sends it back as If-Match.

ConfigSection.description: A part of a config that's saved on its own (putConfigSection): a top-level field that isn't read-only or the server's (`interval`, `timezone`), named as in ConfigResponse. Only those the device's type has: a touchscreen has `clock_format`, `arrivals`, `weather`, `notice_board`, `parcels`, `style`, `display` and `lyrics`.

SearchResult.description: One result of a picker's search (searchStops, searchPlaces), the same in both: what to show (`name` over `subtitle`, indented under the result before it when `indent`) and what picking it saves (`value`, in the config's own shape).

id.description: The result's id at its source, as text.

subtitle.description: The line under it, e.g. what stops there or the place's region and country.

indent.description: Whether it belongs to the result before it (a platform of a station), shown indented under it.

StopSearchResult.description: A station or stop that searchStops found (SearchResult).

area.description: The town or district it's in, to tell stops of the same name apart; may be empty.

mode.description: What it's for, for its icon: tube, metro, tram, rail, water or bus (a bus stop shows its `letter`), or another mode, shown as a bus stop is.

letter.description: Its stop letter or platform code; may be empty.

PlaceSearchResult.description: A town or city that searchPlaces found, for the weather (SearchResult); its `id` is Open-Meteo's.

label.description: Its name, region and country in one line, as the settings site's weather box shows it.

country_code.description: Its country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2); empty when Open-Meteo gives none.

source.description: Who to ask for the stop's departures. tfl is Transport for London; entur is Norway's national journey planner (Ruter and every other Norwegian operator).

id.description: The stop's id at its source. A NaPTAN id for tfl (490000077E, 940GZZLUOVL); an NSR StopPlace or Quay for entur (NSR:StopPlace:58381, NSR:Quay:7333).

enabled.description: Whether the Spotify area shows Apple Music too. Its data comes from the store, in Spotify's shapes, written by the broker's music provider, which holds the Apple token, so no token is sent here. Apple Music has no now playing or queue, so that is what was played last and before it, and top tracks and artists the broker counts from the plays it has seen.
Whether the screen shows the developer panel. Its data comes from the store, which the broker's developer provider fills with the GitHub token it holds, so no token is sent here.
Whether the screen shows the parcels panel and parcel notices. Their data comes from the store, which the parcel provider fills with the Parcel API key it holds, so no key is sent here.
Whether the screen shows the energy panel. Its data comes from the store, which the broker's Glowmarkt provider fills, so no credentials are sent here.

Layout.description: A layout an e-paper screen can be drawn in (EpaperStyle's layout says which sizes have which).

DeviceType.description: What kind of device: an e-paper screen (countdown-esp32), which shows the frames the render pool draws, or a touchscreen, which draws itself from its config.

DeviceRegistration.description: What POST /api/devices/register takes. Every device says its size; an e-paper screen also says the format it takes its frame in (its config's format), while a touchscreen draws itself, so says no format.

secret.description: A random string the device generated and keeps, sent from then on as Authorization: Bearer <secret>. Never logged; the broker keeps only its hash.

type.description: Optional, so a screen that doesn't send it registers as epaper.

width.description: The device's screen width, in pixels.

height.description: The device's screen height, in pixels.

format.description: The format an e-paper screen takes its frame in, as its config's format.

SecretHash.description: A device's secret (DeviceRegistration's), hashed: the hex SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes, in lower case. It's what the broker stores, and doesn't authenticate anything, so it can go in a URL where the secret can't.

ScreenSize.description: A screen's width or height, in pixels.

TouchscreenRegistration.description: What GET /register takes as its query, and its confirming page posts as a form: a touchscreen registering through the login.

return_to.description: A URL of the tablet's own app to come back to, on an origin the server allows; it gets `device_id` (or `error=taken`) added to its query.

ConfigResponse.description: A device's config: the value of v1:config:<device id> (with no pairing code) and, with its pairing_code set, of v1:pairing:<device id>, and what GET and PUT /api/devices/config answer and take. A few flat fields (who and what the device is, its size, and its clock format), then a section per panel, each its own schema, and `style`, which every type has but whose schema is the type's own. A touchscreen's has only what it shows itself: the arrivals, the weather and the notice board, its look, its screen's sleep and its lyrics; an e-paper screen's also has its language, time zone, pairing code and the rest of its panels. `type` says which: an e-paper screen's (EpaperConfig) or a touchscreen's (TouchscreenConfig). It never has a secret of any kind: logins and keys are the owner's account's, held on the server. A read-only field (readOnly) is the server's, or what the device said at registration, and isn't changed by a save.

ConfigBase.description: What every device's config has (ConfigResponse), whatever its type: who and what the device is, its size, its clock format, and the panels both types show (arrivals, weather and the notice board).

width.description: The device's screen width in pixels, as it reported at registration.

height.description: The device's screen height in pixels, as it reported at registration.

clock_format.description: Application-wide format for user-facing clock times. Does not change machine timestamps, durations, time zones or log formats.

EpaperConfig.description: An e-paper screen's config (ConfigResponse with type epaper), which the render pool draws its frames from.

pairing_code.description: The code to show while no one has paired the device: six of A-Z and 2-9, less the look-alikes 0, O, 1, I and L. Only v1:pairing:<device id> has one; null in v1:config:<device id>, and once it's paired.

language.description: The language of everything the device shows, as a BCP 47 code (nb is Norwegian Bokmål).

timezone.description: The device's IANA time zone, e.g. Europe/Oslo, for its clock and what counts as today.

format.description: The format the screen takes its frame in, as it reported at registration (FrameRecord's frame for mono-1bpp-packed).

EpaperStyle.description: How an e-paper screen is drawn.

orientation.description: How the screen hangs; vertical is portrait.

drawing.description: How every panel is drawn, so the screen has one look. airy has small-caps labels over a hairline; hero has an icon header over a heavy rule and makes the first item big; card puts each panel in a rounded card with a black title bar.

weather.description: How the weather is drawn on an HD screen (1872x1404 hung portrait), where it spans the whole width and has room for more than the 7.5" screens' panel. columns puts the readings in tiles beside the conditions, with the outlook under them; timeline has the coming twelve hours in a strip along the bottom; overview shows now, tonight, tomorrow and the weekend side by side, with no tabs; poster sets the temperature very big, with the readings in a black band. Other screens ignore it.

layout.description: Which layout the screen is drawn in, or null for its size's default. Each size of screen has its own layouts, the first its default. A 1872x1404 screen hung portrait has classic (the weather on top, then the stops, Spotify and the notices), masthead (the clock and the weather in a black band across the top), column (the weather down a column beside the stops), lockscreen (a big clock over a card for each panel), timeline (each departure placed by its minute along a line down the middle), board (each route once, with its next three times) and pages (the stops and the rest of the panels on two pages that take turns); hung landscape, sidebar (the clock and the weather in a black sidebar), board (the stops side by side as big departure boards, the weather and the energy chart under them), column (the weather down a column, the stops beside it, then Spotify and the developer panel), focus (each stop's next departure huge, the clock, weather and the rest in a column beside them), newspaper (a front page, the stops, the weather and the notices in columns under a masthead) and pages (as portrait's, side by side in landscape); the 7.5" screens, classic. Hung portrait, both sizes also have the kerbside layouts, the weather in brief over one stop, both big, as track (each route with its departures along a line of the next half hour), ledger (each route once, with the times after the next under where it's going) and queue (every departure on a row of its own). A layout the screen's size doesn't have is drawn as its default.

TouchscreenConfig.description: A touchscreen's config (ConfigResponse with type touchscreen). It draws itself from it, and saves it from its own settings, as its owner does on the settings site. It is English only and paired by token, so it has no language and no pairing code; it keeps its own time, so it has no time zone or interval; and it plays music itself, so it has no music or other integrations' sections but parcels, whose notices join its notice board. Its Wi-Fi stays on the device, never here.

parcels.description: Whether its notice board has the owner's parcels (DeviceNotices.parcels). The server always sends it; null or left out is off, so a config from before it was added reads the same, and a whole save (putConfig) that leaves it out keeps it as it is.

skin.description: day or night, or auto to follow the sun at its location (day from sunrise to sunset), which a touchscreen that doesn't know its location shows as day.

colour.description: The colour, in both skins; violet's play button is a gradient. dynamic is the old dynamic: true, over forest.

dynamic.description: Whether the day skin's colours follow the album art while music plays, fading back to the colour once it has stopped for a while.

sleep_minutes.description: Idle minutes, with no music playing, before the screen sleeps; 0 keeps it on. Only a Raspberry Pi kiosk sleeps its screen: a touchscreen in a browser keeps the setting but ignores it.

TouchscreenLyrics.description: How a touchscreen shows a song's synced lyrics. A config without it (one saved before it existed) shows them at medium size, lined up on the left.

size.description: The lyrics' type size: medium is the size the touchscreen works out from its lyrics panel, and small, large and x-large are 0.8, 1.2 and 1.4 times that.

align.description: Which side the lines line up on.

Arrivals.description: The arrivals panel (bus, train and tram stops).

stops.description: Every stop whose departures the device shows, from any source, in the owner's order.

location.description: The place as the owner named it.

key.description: The key its weather is kept under in the store, v1:weather:<key>; null while no place is set.

NoticeBoard.description: The notice board, of notices about the device's place.

postcode.description: The place's postcode, or null for no local notices.

country.description: The postcode's country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), which decides the local notices, or null with none.

enabled.description: Whether the device shows Spotify. Its data comes from the store, which the server's music provider fills with the account's Spotify link, so no token is sent here.

SpotifyAccessToken.description: A Spotify access token, in the shape Spotify's own token endpoint answers (without its refresh token).

access_token.description: The token, sent to Spotify as Authorization Bearer.

expires_in.description: Seconds until it expires, counted from the answer.

scope.description: The scopes it carries, space-separated, as Spotify granted them: what the settings site's link asks for, which a touchscreen's playback (streaming, user-modify-playback-state and the rest) is part of.

StopDepartures.description: The value of v1:departures:<stop id>: a stop's next departures, whatever the country or mode, in the providers' own shape (TfL's and Entur's answers mapped to one).

stop_id.description: The stop's id at its source (DepartureStop's id).

name.description: As the source names it ("Kennington Underground Station"); a reader shortens it as it likes.

mode.description: The source's own name for the stop's main mode: TfL's bus or tube; Entur's bus, tram, metro, rail, water... (unknown for a stop that lists none).

stop_letter.description: The letter on a London bus stop's flag ("W"), or an Entur quay's code ("2"); null elsewhere.

modes.description: Every mode the stop serves, its main one first, from Entur ([metro, tram]); empty from TfL.

departures.description: Soonest first; empty when nothing is due.

Departure.description: One vehicle due to leave a stop.

destination.description: TfL buses' destination (trimmed at the comma), the Tube's `towards`, Entur's front text.

expected_at.description: When it's due, rather than seconds to go, as a stored value is read some time after it's fetched.

platform.description: The platform or stop pole where the source says: Entur's quay code, TfL's platformName for a Tube train ("Northbound - Platform 1"); null for a TfL bus.

vehicle_id.description: The source's id for the vehicle, the same from one fetch to the next, so a screen can follow it as predictions reorder: TfL's vehicleId (a bus's registration, a train's set number); null where the source has none (Entur).

mode.description: Its mode where a stop serves several (Entur's metro or tram at Majorstuen); null from TfL, whose stops serve one (the stop's `mode`).

scheduled.description: Whether `expected_at` is only the timetable's time, with no live prediction behind it: an Entur call with `realtime` false, or a TfL train or bus from the line's timetable, which the TfL provider adds while TfL predicts nothing for that line at the stop (the first trains of the morning, before the line opens).

StoredForecast.description: The value of v1:weather:<weather key>: a place's Open-Meteo forecast, as fetched (timezone=auto, so its times are the place's local time), in a thin wrapper.

location.description: The weather key it was fetched for (WeatherKey).

OpenMeteoForecast.description: Open-Meteo's forecast answer as the weather provider parsed and wrote it: its sections, each under the provider's own field names (temperature, humidity, wind_speed... rather than Open-Meteo's temperature_2m and the like). `current` has the conditions now (is_day among them), `hourly` and `daily` parallel lists by `time` (daily has each day's sunrise and sunset), `current_units` the units. A reader reads the sections with its own model.

StoredLineStatus.description: The value of v1:notices:tfl-lines:<stop id>: the lines serving a TfL stop, in the order TfL lists them there, each TfL's Line with its lineStatuses (severity, description, reason, validityPeriods) under TfL's own names.

shorts.description: The short forms a model has made of the statuses' reasons here, for a notice's line under its title; one with none (not asked about yet, or refused) isn't listed, and whoever words the notice cuts the text itself.

NoticeShort.description: A provider's own prose (TfL's reason for a line's status, a disruption's description) and the short form a model made of it: stored beside the text it shortens, by the provider that fetched it, so nothing that shows a notice asks a model. It is the provider's words made fewer, not ours, so it's data like the text itself.

text.description: The text it shortens, as the provider wrote it but with each run of whitespace one space: what to match a status's reason or a disruption's text against, squashed the same way.

title.description: What it is and where, in a few words ("Severe delays, Kennington to Morden"). A notice that has a title of its own (a line's, from its name and status) doesn't use it.

summary.description: One line with the most useful detail ("Kennington to Morden, signal failure at Clapham Common").

StoredNetworkStatus.description: The value of v1:notices:tfl-network: every Tube line and the Elizabeth line, in TfL's order, each TfL's Line with its lineStatuses (severity, description, reason, validityPeriods) under TfL's own names.

StoredStationDisruptions.description: The value of v1:notices:tfl-stations:<stop id>: TfL's DisruptedPoints at the stop, under TfL's own names.

shorts.description: The short forms a model has made of the disruptions' descriptions here, for a notice's line under its title; one with none (not asked about yet, or refused) isn't listed, and whoever words the notice cuts the text itself.

StoredRoadDisruptions.description: The value of v1:notices:tfl-roads:<place>: TfL's RoadDisruptions near the postcode's place, under TfL's own names.

postcode.description: The postcode as the broker subscribed it ("SE17 3LL").

shorts.description: The short forms a model has made of the disruptions' comments here, for a notice's line under its title; one with none (not asked about yet, or refused) isn't listed, and whoever words the notice cuts the text itself.

StoredMetOfficeWarnings.description: The value of v1:notices:met-office:<place>: the warnings feed of the Met Office region the postcode is in, as it was at fetched_at.

postcode.description: The postcode it's for, as the broker subscribed it ("SE17 3LL").

region.description: The Met Office warning region whose feed it is ("se"), or UK for the whole of the UK's.

items.description: The feed's items in its order; empty when there are no warnings.

MetOfficeFeedItem.description: One item of the Met Office's warnings feed, its elements' text as the feed has it ("" for one it lacks).

title.description: The warning's colour, kind and region ("Amber warning of wind affecting London & South East").

description.description: Where and when ("...: Lambeth, Southwark valid from 0600 Fri 25 Sep to 2100 Fri 25 Sep").

link.description: The warning's page on the Met Office's site.

pub_date.description: When it was published, as the feed writes it (RFC 822, "Thu, 24 Sep 2026 10:30:00 GMT").

StoredBackground.description: The value of v1:background:<weather key>: the AI-made photos behind a place's weather panel, one per part of its day, for the place's local date.

location.description: The weather key they were made for (WeatherKey).

local_date.description: The place's local date they are for.

images.description: Those made so far, in the order of `starts_at`. A screen shows the last whose `starts_at` has passed, and before the first, the night image of the day before if it still has it.

Background.description: One part of the day's background.

starts_at.description: When it starts showing, with its offset: dawn 30 minutes before sunrise, day 90 minutes after it, dusk an hour before sunset and night 45 minutes after it, from the forecast's daily sunrise and sunset.

fallback.description: True when generating failed and this is one of the curated pictures instead, so the screen can tell and the provider can try again.

BackgroundPlace.description: The value of v1:background-place:<weather key>: a place the paired touchscreens show, as the background provider needs it.

name.description: What to call the place in a picture's prompt: its full label as picked on the settings page ("London, England, United Kingdom"), else its name, else the location as typed.

country.description: Its two-letter country code ("GB"), or null when it has none (a typed location, not yet placed).

postcodes.description: The postcodes of the notice boards of the touchscreens showing the place, in the broker's canonical form ("SE17 3LL"), sorted; empty when none has one. Never logged.

BackgroundPhase.description: The part of the day a background is lit for.

BackgroundDigest.description: A background image's SHA-256, in lower-case hex, which names it in its key and its address.

BackgroundImage.description: A background image file's own bytes (a JPEG).

StoredBankHolidays.description: The value of v1:notices:bank-holidays, gov.uk's bank holidays for every part of the UK.

divisions.description: By gov.uk's name for each part of the UK; England and Wales share one.

BankHolidayDivision.description: One part of the UK's bank holidays.

notes.description: Such as "Substitute day"; empty for most.

DeviceFeedEvent.description: One event of getFeed's stream, by its name: `weather` with a DeviceWeather, `arrivals` with a DeviceArrivals or `notices` with a DeviceNotices, each what that route would answer at the time. On the wire it is the event's `event:` line and its data as one `data:` line of JSON.

DeviceWeather.description: A device's weather (getWeather): its config's place, and the place's stored forecast as v1:weather:<key> has it.

location.description: The place as the owner named it (the config's weather.location).

key.description: The config's weather.key; null while no place is set.

forecast.description: The forecast, or null with no place set or none stored for it (its provider is down, or new).

background.description: The place's backgrounds as v1:background:<key> has them, or null with no place set or none made yet. Each image is at getBackgroundImage's /api/backgrounds/<digest>.

DeviceArrivals.description: A device's live arrivals (getArrivals), for every stop in its config, in the owner's order.

StopArrivals.description: One of a device's stops, and its departures as v1:departures:<stop id> has them.

departures.description: The stop's departures, or null with none stored (its provider is down, or the stop is new).

DeviceNotices.description: A device's notices (getNotices), as the store has them: what the notice board makes its notices from, not the notices themselves. A source that doesn't apply to the device is empty or null (TfL's for a device with no TfL stops; the Met Office's, TfL's roads and the bank holidays for one whose postcode isn't a UK one), as is one with nothing stored.

tfl_stops.description: Each of the device's TfL stops, in the owner's order.

bank_holidays.description: Every part of the UK's; the postcode's place says which applies.

tfl_network.description: Every Tube line's status and the Elizabeth line's, for a device with a TfL stop or a UK postcode; null for any other, or with none stored.

parcels.description: The owner's parcels as the parcel provider stored them (v1:parcels:<device id>), already narrowed to those the device's settings show, for a device with parcels switched on; null for any other, or with none stored. The device makes its notices from them as the e-paper notice board does.

TflStopNotices.description: A TfL stop's line statuses and station disruptions, each null with none stored.
